briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Bipartisan Tax Revolt Builds in Lansing While DC Clears the Runway for Rescheduling and Psilocybin
briefs.top: Michigan's governor's race just turned into a referendum on the 24% wholesale weed tax, with both major-party contenders now pledging to gut it — real political momentum for operators grinding through a brutal year. Nationally, DEA's rescheduling machine keeps grinding forward and Compass Pathways just put psilocybin on a fast track to FDA approval, giving the whole plant-medicine sector a genuine growth story heading into fall.

local.text: State Rep. James DeSana introduced HB 6224 to fully repeal the 24% wholesale tax, arguing it's unconstitutional and already hammering the industry; the bill was referred to House Appropriations and reproduced by the Legislature on August 11 — the second repeal bill this year after Sen. Jonathan Lindsey's bipartisan SB 810.

GOP gubernatorial nominee John James unveiled a platform August 19 pledging to repeal or sharply reduce the wholesale tax, calling it a giveaway to illegal operators — joining Democratic primary contender Chris Swanson, who's already campaigning on rolling it back, meaning whoever wins in November has publicly committed to relief.

Despite the new tax, Michigan dispensary demand hasn't collapsed — inventory data shows retailers, processors and growers sitting on nearly two years' worth of flower supply, and February's sales dip was driven by falling prices rather than falling demand, per state regulators.

A new Michigan Supreme Court ruling means police can no longer search a car based solely on the smell of marijuana, closing off a common pretext stop that's dogged legal consumers and store customers statewide.

The pressure is real: Higher Love Cannabis Co. shut five of its nine Upper Peninsula stores (Crystal Falls, Escanaba, Houghton, Munising, Ontonagon) on August 9, citing the wholesale tax directly — the exact scenario driving MiCIA's two pending lawsuits and the fresh legislative repeal push.

national.text: DEA's marijuana rescheduling process cleared another procedural checkpoint on August 18, keeping the multi-year push to move cannabis from Schedule I to Schedule III on track — a shift that would slash 280E tax rates from roughly 60% to the mid-20s for operators.

Compass Pathways' psilocybin therapy COMP360 is now riding an FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher that compresses review to just 1-2 months; the company is targeting a Q4 2026 rolling NDA submission with analysts eyeing approval as early as late 2026.

FDA finalized its clinical trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA, directly addressing the functional-unblinding problem that sank Lykos Therapeutics' MDMA application in 2024 — and set a public hearing on psychedelic therapeutic use for September 14, 2026.

Cannabis M&A is accelerating fast: Vireo Growth's all-stock deal for Planet 13 (announced July 27) would push it to roughly 265 dispensaries across 15 states, making it the largest U.S. cannabis retailer by store count as consolidators snap up distressed assets.

The shakeout has a flip side for buyers: Cannabist's bankruptcy is freeing up inventory and facilities — including New Jersey cultivation sites being wound down — for aggressive acquirers like Vireo and SNDL to absorb into bigger, leaner platforms.
